confirmed.location: CityLayoutBuilder.Compute(), lines 85-224 (districtCount derived at 85; bounds computed at 187-224) combined with CityBuilder.cs BuildGround() lines 152-167
confirmed.summary: When a repo has zero files, districtCount is 0, so the bounds-accumulation loop never runs and minX/maxX/minZ/maxZ are left at their float.MaxValue/float.MinValue sentinel seeds, producing an inverted CityBounds that downstream code turns into an infinite/negative ground-plane scale.
confirmed.failureScenario: Load a repo-data.json with "files": [] (an empty repo, or a repo whose entire file list got filtered out upstream). CityLayoutBuilder.Compute returns bounds.minX = float.MaxValue, bounds.maxX = float.MinValue (inverted). CityBuilder.BuildGround then computes sizeX = (bounds.maxX - bounds.minX) + 80, which overflows float range to -Infinity, and sets the ground plane's localScale.x/z to -Infinity instead of failing loudly or falling back to a sane default size - the scene ends up with a broken/invisible ground and Unity transform warnings instead of a usable (even if empty) city.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed by reading both files directly and tracing the arithmetic.

In CityLayout.cs, `CityLayoutBuilder.Compute()`: if `data.files` is empty (e.g. `"files": []` in repo-data.json, which `RepoDataLoader.Load()` happily deserializes via `JsonUtility.FromJson` with no null/empty check — see RepoData.cs lines 34-45), then the `foreach (FileEntry file in data.files)` loop at line 54 never executes, so `districtKeys` stays empty and `districtCount = districtKeys.Count` (line 85) is 0.

All subsequent loops keyed on `districtCount` (lines 95, 121-150, 153-184, 190-201) are no-ops. The bounds-accumulation loop at lines 190-201 never runs, so `minX`/`maxX`/`minZ`/`maxZ` keep their sentinel seed values from line 187-188: `minX = float.MaxValue`, `maxX = float.MinValue` (and same for Z).

Then `centerX = (minX + maxX) * 0.5f` (line 203): since C# `float.MinValue == -float.MaxValue` exactly, this sums to 0, so `centerX = 0` (same for `centerZ`). The final bounds (lines 217-223) become `minX = float.MaxValue - 0 = float.MaxValue`, `maxX = float.MinValue - 0 = float.MinValue` — i.e. inverted (`minX > maxX`), exactly as claimed.

In CityBuilder.cs `BuildGround()` (lines 152-167): `sizeX = (bounds.maxX - bounds.minX) + GroundMargin*2f` evaluates to `float.MinValue - float.MaxValue + 80f`. `float.MinValue - float.MaxValue` is approximately `-6.8e38`, which exceeds the finite float range and overflows to `float.NegativeInfinity`; adding 80 leaves it at `-Infinity`. This is then divided by `UnityPlaneDefaultSize` (10f) at line 163 and assigned directly to `ground.transform.localScale.x` (and `.z` via the analogous `sizeZ`) with no sanity check or clamping anywhere in between.

No caller (SceneBootstrapper.cs line 23, WorldBuilder.cs line 28) guards against `data.files.Count == 0` before calling `Compute()`, and nothing in RepoData.cs/RepoDataLoader rejects an empty `files` array — a syntactically valid repo-data.json with `"files": []` reaches this code path unmodified. The finding's file, line ranges, root cause, and failure scenario all check out against the actual source; this is a real, reachable bug, not a misread.

verdict.reasoning: Read CityBuilder.cs lines 90-166 directly. confirmed.location: WorldBuilder.BuildAll(), lines 55-61 (interacts with CarFollower.Update in TrafficController.cs and NpcWalker.Update in NpcController.cs)
confirmed.summary: Traffic and pedestrian loop waypoints are captured in the island's pre-shift (local-origin) coordinate frame, then the island is moved to its real worldCenter afterward, leaving every car/NPC chasing stale, wrongly-offset target points on every island except the first.
confirmed.failureScenario: In the World Hub scene with 2+ islands (e.g. the three-city setup), WorldBuilder.Build loop does: TrafficSpawner.Spawn(islandRoot.transform, roads.carLoopWaypoints, CarCount) and NpcSpawner.Spawn(...) while islandRoot is still at local (0,0,0) (line 55-56), THEN sets islandRoot.transform.localPosition = worldCenter (line 61). CarFollower (TrafficController.cs Initialize/Update) and NpcWalker (NpcController.cs Init/Update) store the raw waypoint list by reference and every frame compute `target - transform.position` using WORLD-space transform.position. Because the car/NPC GameObjects are children of islandRoot, Unity's hierarchy correctly shifts their actual world position when islandRoot moves, but the cached `waypoints` list is never re-offset by worldCenter. For every island whose worldCenter != Vector3.zero (i.e. every island but the home/first one - the only one actually screenshotted), the per-frame direction vector is off by a constant -worldCenter (can be hundreds of meters, since worldCenter.x accumulates halfWidth+IslandGap per island), so cars and pedestrians don't loop their ring road/sidewalk at all - they drive/walk in a straight line off toward world origin and out of their own city, with the arrival checks (ArrivalThreshold/WaypointArriveDistance) never meaningfully triggering since the offset dwarfs them.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed by reading WorldBuilder.cs, TrafficController.cs, and NpcController.cs directly.

WorldBuilder.BuildAll (lines 55-56) calls TrafficSpawner.Spawn(islandRoot.transform, roads.carLoopWaypoints, CarCount) and NpcSpawner.Spawn(islandRoot.transform, roads.sidewalkLoopWaypoints, NpcCount) while islandRoot is still at local/world (0,0,0) — the shift to worldCenter happens only afterward, at line 61 (`islandRoot.transform.localPosition = worldCenter`).

Inside TrafficSpawner.Spawn (TrafficController.cs), each car is instantiated as a child of islandRoot and CarFollower.Initialize() is called with the raw `carLoopWaypoints` list (stored by reference as `waypoints`) and sets `transform.position = waypoints[startIndex]` (world-space setter, but islandRoot is still at origin so this is numerically the pre-shift/local value). Identical pattern for NpcSpawner/NpcWalker in NpcController.cs.

When WorldBuilder later sets islandRoot.transform.localPosition = worldCenter (line 61), Unity's parent-child hierarchy correctly shifts every child's actual world position by +worldCenter (parenting preserves local offsets, so moving the parent moves all children automatically) — but the `waypoints` list cached inside each CarFollower/NpcWalker is the *same list reference* as roads.carLoopWaypoints/sidewalkLoopWaypoints, which is never re-offset; WorldBuilder only builds a *new*, separately-shifted list (lines 63-64, `carWaypointsWorld`/`sidewalkWaypointsWorld`) that goes into the returned WorldIslandResult and is never handed back to the already-spawned CarFollower/NpcWalker components.

So in CarFollower.Update / NpcWalker.Update, `target = waypoints[targetIndex]` uses the stale pre-shift coordinates while `transform.position` is now the real shifted world position for every island except the first (worldCenter == Vector3.zero only for isFirst). The resulting `toTarget = target - transform.position` is off by a constant `-worldCenter` every frame, so on any island beyond the first, cars/NPCs are driven by a direction vector dominated by that constant offset rather than the real local waypoint delta — exactly the reported defect. This matches the report's own caveat that only the first/home island was ever screenshotted, which is consistent since that is the one island where worldCenter is zero and the bug would be invisible.

confirmed.location: locomotion.OnInspect / locomotion.OnInteractNpc handlers, lines 88-118 (StartCoroutine calls at 98 and 113); identical pattern in WorldBootstrapper.cs lines 75-102 (StartCoroutine at 85 and 97)
confirmed.summary: A stale narration/NPC-chat coroutine from a previous inspection is never stopped when superseded - only its eventual callback result is discarded via the inspectToken check - so the coroutine (and whatever network/IO call it wraps inside OllamaNarrator.GetNarration / NpcChat.GetLine) keeps running to completion regardless.
confirmed.failureScenario: Player grip-presses building after building (or building then NPC then building) in quick succession, e.g. walking down a street holding grip near several facades within a few seconds. Each inspect bumps inspectToken and calls StartCoroutine without cancelling the previous one, so N rapid inspections leave N concurrent in-flight coroutines/requests running simultaneously even though only the last one's result will ever be shown; on a VR headset doing frequent inspect gestures, or if OllamaNarrator's underlying call is slow/blocking-ish, this accumulates outstanding work and network/IO pressure that never gets cancelled, only discarded after the fact.

verdict.reasoning:
Read SceneBootstrapper.cs lines 86-118 directly, plus OllamaNarrator.cs and NpcChat.cs (the coroutines being started), plus WorldBootstrapper.cs lines 70-110 for the parallel claim.

The finding is accurate. In both OnInspect and OnInteractNpc handlers, each call does: inspectToken++; capture token; then `StartCoroutine(...)` without ever retaining a reference to the previous Coroutine object or calling StopCoroutine on it. The `token == inspectToken` check inside the completion callback only gates whether the *result* gets written to the HUD — it does nothing to halt the coroutine's execution up to that point.

Critically, OllamaNarrator.GetNarration and NpcChat.GetLine are not cheap/instant coroutines — each does a real two-step UnityWebRequest sequence: first a GET ping to http://localhost:11434/api/tags (1s timeout), then if successful, a POST to /api/generate with a 3s timeout, both awaited via `yield return request.SendWebRequest()`. These are real asynchronous network calls that continue running on Unity's web request system regardless of whether `inspectToken` has since changed.

So the claimed scenario holds: if a player grip-inspects several buildings (or buildings then NPCs) in quick succession — well within the ~1-3s request latency window — each inspect increments inspectToken and fires a brand new StartCoroutine/UnityWebRequest pair with no cancellation of the prior one. N rapid inspections produce N concurrent in-flight UnityWebRequest pairs, of which only the result matching the final (latest) token will ever be displayed; the other N-1 run to completion or timeout purely to be discarded. This is wasted network/IO work that scales with how fast the player can trigger inspects, with no cap or debounce.

The identical pattern (same StartCoroutine-without-stop structure, same inspectToken-only gating, calling the same OllamaNarrator.GetNarration / NpcChat.GetLine coroutines) is also present in WorldBootstrapper.cs's OnInspect/OnInteractNpc handlers (confirmed at lines 83-118), matching the finding's claim that it's duplicated there.

Nothing in the code already handles this (no StopCoroutine, no request.Abort(), no debounce/cooldown on the inspect gesture, no reuse of a single Coroutine handle). So this is a real, concrete, currently-unmitigated resource/lifecycle issue as described, not a misread.
